Mogielnica Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mogielnica, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Mogielnica developed after 1779, and in the following century the town became the seat of the Mogelnitz Hasidic dynasty. By 1921, 2,722 Jews made up over half the population, most murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery was established at the end of the 18th century and enlarged around 1862; in 1849, its founding Rebbe, Chaim Meir Jechiel Szapira, was buried there. During the war, Germans used tombstones to harden a gendarmerie courtyard, and locals stole others for construction. Around 2002, Hasidic communities funded two ohels - a larger one over the Rebbe's presumed grave alongside his parents and wife, and a smaller one for Rebbe Jakow of Mogielnica. A 2012 archaeological excavation uncovered the dynasty's actual burial locations along with several tombstones retaining original polychrome paint. Stolen tombstones recovered from the former gendarmerie courtyard were later placed inside the ohel, and a monitoring system was installed for ongoing protection.
